newsitem.title: USA: UAW union opposes Clinton on China trade status.
newsitem.headline: UAW union opposes Clinton on China trade status.

text.p: The United Auto Workers union opposes President Clinton's recommendation that China's most-favored-nation trade status be extended for one year, UAW President Stephen Yokich said Wednesday.
"China's abysmal record of disregard for basic human rights and fair labor standards is reason enough not to renew that nation's MFN status," Yokich said in a statement.

"The hard reality is that the administration's strategy of engagement has been a total failure in terms of influencing the Chinese government to take even the smallest steps toward a more open and free society," he said.
In addition to human rights issues, Yokich said China had "unfair and discriminatory" trade and industrial policies that threatened jobs in the U.S. auto and aerospace industries.
"While the UAW has supported President Clinton on many issues, on the issue of renewing China's MFN status we believe the President's position is simply wrong," Yokich said.
The UAW is urging Congress to reject the extension, he said.
